instructions: You turn a video of a hands-on task into a step procedure with evidence. Every step names what the camera can see that proves it was done, and names what the camera cannot verify. Use the video's timeline in seconds. Be concrete: nouns a segmentation model could track. Rate each checkpoint's visibility honestly: a checkpoint you know only from the narration is narration_only, even if the step surely happened. One step per place or part: when the hands move to a different edge, side, corner or part, start a new step, even if the action repeats, so that skipping any one place shows as a missing step. Only steps the hands perform on the task: leave out title cards, screenshots, on-screen text, close-ups that only show a label, and pointing at parts.

The Liberator is built from stock steel, hydraulic components and an optional automated control unit, with material costs under $4,000 for the fully automated machine. Steel materials require fabrication using standard tools found in any well equipped metal shop. This video will demonstrate the correct assembly of all steel parts of the Liberator CEB Press, once they have been acquired and fabricated. Hydraulic and automatic control unit assembly guides are not included in this video, but can be found on the Open Source Ecology wiki. Before continuing, please be aware that the CEB Press is a large, heavy machine. Assembly should take place on a flat, stable surface, with constant attention paid to the assembled pieces until they are secured. At least two people and a heavy duty hoist should be available to complete the assembly. If a hoist is unavailable, additional people will be required. Anyone involved in this assembly must wear a hard hat, eye protection and gloves to avoid personal injury. Please exercise caution and common sense during the entire assembly process. First, ensure you have all parts ready for the assembly. Parts for the base, hopper and grate assemblies include hopper, grate with front and side soil deflectors, shaker assembly, hopper seat, secondary cylinder, feet, legs, primary arms, secondary arms, hopper support holders, hopper supports, cam rollers, hopper support holders, hopper supports, cam rollers, sensor holder. Parts for the main frame assembly include vertical frame members, primary cylinder, cylinder mount plates, top frame plates, compression chamber cover plates, compression chamber chamber spacers. The Liberator has two ends that serve different functions. The loading side of the Liberator is the end from which soil is loaded into the hopper. Sides of the Liberator will be referred to in this fashion throughout this assembly video. Step 1 Main Frame Assembly. Lay out the main frame pieces on the ground. Bolt the compression chamber spacers to the vertical frame members. Attach one cylinder mount plate and top frame plate to the vertical frame members and stand the frame up. Bolt on the second cylinder mount and top frame plates, and insert the primary hydraulic cylinder with cylinder mount plate and secure with pin. Now attach the compression chamber cover plates. This completes the main frame assembly. Step 2 Base Assembly. Clear an open area and place the four legs in the four feet. Next, insert the legs into the outer leg holders on the secondary arms for the loading side and ejection side of the machine. Note that placement of the secondary arm with the central welded tabs dictates the loading side of the machine. Next, attach the primary arms to the secondary arms. Ensure the midway bolt holes on both primary arms align. The position of these bolt holes must be biased towards the ejection side of the base assembly. Use a hoist to lower the main frame assembly between the primary arms. Ensure the main frame assembly is placed by the midway bolt holes on the primary arms with its width parallel to the primary arms so the base assembly can be raised around it. An alternate procedure is to attach only one primary arm to the secondary arms, raise the three arms to the required height, shuffle the frame assembly into place, and attach the remaining arm around the frame. This avoids the need to use a hoist. It is important to tighten the bolts in the leg mounts firmly before proceeding. Now pivot the main frame assembly so the bolt holes align with the four midway bolt holes on the primary arms. Bolt these together securely. Next, mount the drawer into the main frame assembly such that the one inch by three inch rail arm is up. Now attach the base of the secondary cylinder to the central welded tabs on the secondary arm on the loading side of the machine. Attach the piston of the secondary cylinder to the tabs on the drawer. Now attach the four cam roller assemblies to the primary arms. Slide each of the four arms of the drawer onto a cam roller and secure the cam roller assemblies to the primary arms. This completes the base assembly. audio_notes.description: non-speech sounds that carry information, or 'none'

speech_heard.description: transcript of any speech in the audio track, or 'none'

action.description: one verb phrase, what the hands do

cannot_see.description: a property of this step the camera cannot verify, or 'none'

checkpoint_visibility.description: clear: the checkpoint is plainly visible in the frames; subtle: visible only briefly, partly, small or occluded; narration_only: known from the speech, not visible

evidence_s.description: the second in this video where the checkpoint is best seen

objects.description: parts and tools involved, as concrete noun phrases a segmentation model can track

observable_checkpoint.description: what a camera can see that shows the step was done

track.description: up to four noun phrases, copied exactly from the steps' objects, whose position in the frame shows the task progressing: the tools first, then the parts that move; never hands or gloves, not the whole workpiece, not the background
